name: The Key
version: v1.3 · 2026-11-18 · pull facts from a policy, papers attached on the phone (s19–s28) · store step: free
intro:
⚠️ BEFORE STEP 1 — check you are in a test copy. Look for the small “🧪 Test copy” mark on the screen. It means this app has never seen you, which is what the steps below expect. If it is missing and the app already shows your own information, you have opened your real app: go back to your list and tap this app's name again, rather than using a bookmark, your history, or an icon on your home screen. Starting in the wrong copy makes the early steps look broken when nothing is wrong.

You will fill in a few made-up lines about where things are kept, watch the ✓ marks and the progress bar change, check that it all stays after a reload and with no internet, look at the print preview, then pull the facts out of a made-up policy with your own AI and attach a photo to a line. Please use only the example words — never real passwords or account numbers.

steps.do: Look at the welcome card at the bottom (“Welcome to The Key”). Tap the small words “skip the tour” at its bottom right.
steps.see: A new card asks how you want to start, with two big choices: “🧪 Keep the examples to play with” and “✨ Start fresh with my own”.
steps.tip: A green greeting strip may also show at the top (for example “Good morning.”). Tap its ✕ if it is in the way.

steps.do: Tap “✨ Start fresh with my own”.
steps.see: The card goes away straight away (the app has nothing to clear, so it does not ask). Near the top it says “Nothing filled in yet — start anywhere.” If a box does ask “Start fresh? The examples will be cleared.”, tap OK.

steps.do: If “📷 My pictures live here” is closed, tap it to open it.
steps.see: The first section, “📷 My pictures live here”, is open.

steps.do: Scroll down past the five sections and tap the big “🖨 Print my Key” button, before you have written anything.
steps.see: Nothing prints. A box says “Fill in at least one section first — even one line helps them someday.” Tap OK.

steps.do: Scroll back up. In “📷 My pictures live here”, tap “＋ Add a place your pictures live”.
steps.see: A panel slides up titled “Add a place your pictures live”, with choices like Phone, iCloud Photos, Google Photos, Computer and Photo albums.
steps.tip: If the panel’s Save button is hidden at the bottom of the screen, that is a known problem, already reported — just close the panel in the next step.

steps.do: Tap the dim strip at the very top of the screen, above the panel.
steps.see: The panel closes and you are back on the page. Nothing new was added.

steps.do: Still in “📷 My pictures live here”, tap the box under “Other notes (optional)” and type this example.
steps.type: Old photo albums are in the hall closet, top shelf (example)
steps.see: Your words are in the box, and “✓ started” appears on the right of the “📷 My pictures live here” heading.

steps.do: Scroll down and tap the heading “💌 Anything else they should know” to open it.
steps.see: It opens. It says “A wish, an instruction, a kindness. In your own words.” and has a box with grey example words about the dog’s vet.

steps.do: Tap that box and type this example (with the apostrophe).
steps.type: Margaret O'Brien has the spare house key. (example)
steps.see: The apostrophe in O'Brien looks right, “✓ started” appears next to “💌 Anything else they should know”, and the bar at the top now says “Your Key: 2 of 5 sections started · 40% of the boxes filled in”.
steps.tip: Two sections, not one — “📷 My pictures live here” was started back at step 7 and this is the second. If the bar says 1 of 5 · 20%, the step 7 note did not save; scroll up and check it is still there.

steps.do: Pull the page down to reload it (or tap ↻ in Safari).
steps.see: Both of your lines are still there — the hall closet note and the Margaret O'Brien note — each with “✓ started” next to its heading. No welcome card comes back.

steps.do: Tap the heading “💻 My accounts that matter” to open it.
steps.see: It opens and says “The accounts your family would need to find or close. Never the password itself.” with a “＋ Add an account” button.

steps.do: Turn on Airplane Mode (swipe down from the top-right corner, tap ✈️). Then tap the “Other notes (optional)” box in “💻 My accounts that matter” and type this example.
steps.type: Bank statements are in the blue folder in the desk (example)
steps.see: It still works with no internet: your words stay in the box and “✓ started” appears next to “💻 My accounts that matter”.

steps.do: Turn Airplane Mode off. Then pull the page down to reload it.
steps.see: The blue folder note is still there, so it was saved even with no internet.

steps.do: Scroll down and tap “🖨 Print my Key”.
steps.see: A print preview opens: a clean page headed “🔑 The Key” with “Updated” and today’s date, then each section in capitals (“📷 MY PICTURES LIVE HERE”, “💻 MY ACCOUNTS THAT MATTER” …) with your lines under them and a “—” under the empty ones. The buttons are not on it (in the test copy a plain purple strip may print at the bottom). Tap Cancel.

steps.do: Scroll to the bottom and tap “Start over”.
steps.see: A box asks “Clear everything and start over?”. Tap Cancel — nothing is erased.

steps.do: Scroll back to the top of the page.
steps.see: Your three example lines are still there, with “✓ started” next to 📷 My pictures live here, 💻 My accounts that matter and 💌 Anything else they should know.

steps.do: Scroll up and tap the heading “📄 Important papers” to open it.
steps.see: It opens with a “＋ Add an important paper” button, and under it a second button, “📄 Pull facts from a policy”.

steps.do: Tap “📄 Pull facts from a policy”.
steps.see: A panel slides up called “📄 Pull facts from a policy”. A yellow box says “🔒 Never paste a password.” and that your AI gives back only the last 4 digits of any number. Under it are a “Step 1 — the paper’s words” box with “✨ Ask my AI to pull the facts”, and a “Step 2 — paste what your AI said” box.

steps.do: Tap the Step 1 box and type the made-up policy below.
steps.type: Homeowners policy declarations. Insurer: Hometown Mutual Insurance. Policy number HM-5520-8817. Policy period March 1 2026 to March 1 2027. Your agent: Bob Miller, 555-0142. (example)
steps.see: The words are in the box.

steps.do: Tap “✨ Ask my AI to pull the facts”. If it asks “Which AI do you use?”, tap yours (Claude if you are not sure). Then tap the big button. If it said “Send it →”, just wait. If it opened Claude (or ChatGPT), let it answer, copy the WHOLE answer, come back to The Key, paste it into “Paste the answer” and tap “Use this answer”.
steps.see: A panel called “📄 Check the facts” opens. “Insurance policy” is picked, the insurer says Hometown Mutual Insurance, the number box shows only the last 4: “8817”, and the date is 2027-03-01. At the bottom, “Also add to 🤝 The people who know things” is ticked, with Bob Miller as Insurance agent.
steps.tip: If the number box ever shows more than 4 characters, or anything that looks like a password, that is a real fault: say so.

steps.do: In “Where the paper is kept”, type the example below. Then tap “Save to my Key”.
steps.see: The panel closes and a note says “✓ Saved to 📄 Important papers and 🤝 The people who know things”. Under Important papers there is an “Insurance policy” line ending “No. ending 8817 · Renews 2027-03-01”, and “🤝 The people who know things” now shows Bob Miller.

steps.do: On that “Insurance policy” line, tap “Edit”, then scroll down the panel to “📎 The paper itself (optional)”.
steps.see: It says “Nothing attached yet.”, with a “📎 Add a photo or PDF” button and the words “It stays on this phone only, up to 12 MB. “💾 Save a copy” does not include it, so keep the original.”

steps.do: Tap “📎 Add a photo or PDF” and take a photo of any piece of paper (or choose one from your photos).
steps.see: The photo shows in the list with its size, a “View” button and an ✕.
steps.tip: Use a photo of something harmless, like a receipt or a page of a magazine. Never a real policy or anything with a password on it.

steps.do: Tap “View”.
steps.see: Your photo shows large on a dark screen, with “Open full size” and “Close”. Tap “Close”.

steps.do: Tap “Save” at the bottom of the panel. Then scroll to the “💾 Save a copy” buttons near the bottom of the page.
steps.see: The Insurance policy line now ends “· 📎 1 paper attached on the phone”. Just under the Save a copy buttons a line says photos and PDFs you attach stay on this phone only and “💾 Save a copy” does not include them.

steps.do: Tap “🖨 Print my Key”.
steps.see: In the print preview, under 📄 IMPORTANT PAPERS, the Insurance policy line says “📎 1 paper attached on the phone”, and near the bottom of the page it says “📎 One line has papers attached on the phone”. Tap Cancel.

steps.do: Now the videos. This app has 3. Open each one and watch it right through, sound on: Explain it to me — https://jerrywins1.github.io/daraja-apps/shop/watch.html?app=thekey&mode=firsttime  Watch it work — https://jerrywins1.github.io/daraja-apps/shop/watch.html?app=thekey  Train me — https://jerrywins1.github.io/daraja-apps/shop/watch.html?app=thekey&mode=train
steps.see: Each one talks without stopping — no long silences, no sentence starting again. The screen behind the words changes to match what is being said, and when it points at something, that thing is really there. If a video talks about a button or a screen you did not see in this app, say so — that is a real fault and one of the most useful things you can find.

steps.do: Last, the shop page everyone sees before they buy: https://jerrywins1.github.io/daraja-apps/shop/ — find this app on its shelf and read its card.
steps.see: The name and the one-line description match the app you just used. The price says Free, with an optional donation to Loving InDeed. That is right: nothing is sold, and nobody has to give. Nothing on the card promises something the app does not do. If the card and the app disagree, the card is the fault — say which bit.
